_readme: The menu of wave sets a story writer can pick from with a WAVES: line.
Writers never edit this file - they pick a name from HOW-TO-WRITE-A-CHAPTER.md.
A wave set is an ordered sequence of boards that arrive DURING the battle, one at a time.
text is printed word for word on the pre-battle brief, above the schedule: the player is never surprised.
side says whose board the waves land on. Waves arrive strictly in order, at most one per turn.
characters are CARD NAMES, exactly as printed on the card - not ids. A misspelling is reported with the closest name that would have worked.
A wave needs at least one cue. onBoardClear: true arrives once that side has no characters left; onTurn: n arrives on their nth turn. Both means whichever comes first.
Wave characters are DEALT, not played: nothing in a wave costs Hype, counts as a card played, or fires an on-play effect. They arrive with summoning sickness unless the entry says ready: true.
A wave may not be larger than the board (6 characters), because the surplus would have nowhere to stand.
Any key starting with an underscore is a note and is ignored.

the-support-queue.name: The Support Queue
the-support-queue.text: The queue arrives in three bands, on the schedule the rollout is on. A band lands as soon as their side of the board is empty — and lands anyway, on the day it was scheduled for, if it is not.
_note: Written for Chapter 9, Episode 4. The labels are the chapter's own prose:
band one at nine, band two at noon, band three on Thursday, two days after
everybody has stopped watching for it.
Band one is scheduled only - it goes out at nine whatever the board looks
like, and the board is empty on turn one anyway. Bands two and three lead
with the board-clear cue and keep a date as a backstop, so a player who
ignores the board and races the leader still meets the whole rollout.
Nine bodies across a match sounds like a lot and is not, because the
board-clear cue can only fire on a board the player has already cleared:
the reward for winning the board is more board. Nothing here is bigger
than a 4/4, and nothing arrives able to attack.
